mainTopic: Which kinds of מילה override שבת: the drasha of the word ערלתו, the cases of אנדרוגינוס, a child born בין השמשות, a child born מהול, and a ספק בן שבעה or בן שמונה.
overview: The amud continues a ברייתא that learns from the word ערלתו that only a definite מילה overrides שבת. The first תנא excludes a ספק case and an אנדרוגינוס. רבי יהודה holds that an אנדרוגינוס's מילה does override שבת, and he uses the word to exclude a baby born בין השמשות and a baby born already circumcised. About that baby, בית שמאי and בית הלל argue whether דם ברית must be drawn. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says everyone requires it because of ערלה כבושה, and the real argument is about a גר who was circumcised before converting. The גמרא explains that 'ספק' refers to a baby who may be a בן שמונה, who is also treated like a stone on שבת. רב and שמואל argue over whose version of the מחלוקת is the הלכה. The story of רב אדא בר אהבה's son then leads to the question of whether the hidden foreskin is a doubt (רבה) or a certainty (רב יוסף), and the גמרא shows that רב יוסף's proof from רבי אליעזר הקפר is not conclusive. Finally, רבי אסי links eighth-day מילה to the mother's טומאת לידה, and אביי challenges him from the generations before מתן תורה. רבי אסי begins his answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A doubtful מילה does not override שבת
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא's first drasha: only a definite foreskin overrides שבת, not a doubtful one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a doubtful [case of מילה] does not push aside שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the ברייתא in the middle. It has just learned from the word ערלתו that a definite מילה overrides שבת, and here it finishes the thought: a ספק case does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ערלתו ('HIS foreskin') is read as limiting: it must clearly be a foreskin that needs cutting on this exact day. When there is real doubt, the normal rule against doing מלאכה on שבת stays in force. The גמרא will come back to this line in step 9 and ask which case it includes.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt; an uncertain case
Pushes aside שבת (it is allowed to be done on שבת even though it involves מלאכה)
Definite; certain

phrases.english: and a doubtful [case] does not override Shabbat.
phrases.notes: This finishes the drasha of ערלתו that began on the previous amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא סָפֵק דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the drasha begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ספק מילה does not override שבת.

steps.title: An אנדרוגינוס's מילה does not override שבת
steps.stepSummary: The first תנא uses ערלתו again to exclude an אנדרוגינוס from overriding שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'ערלתו': a definite [foreskin] overrides שבת, but [the מילה of] an אנדרוגינוס does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats the same drasha of ערלתו and applies it to a new case: an אנדרוגינוס, a baby with both male and female features.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אנדרוגינוס is not clearly a 'he', so ערלתו ('HIS foreskin') does not clearly apply to him. Because his status is unclear, his מילה does not push aside שבת. He is still circumcised, but on a weekday.

keyTerms.meaning: A hermaphrodite: a person with both male and female features
'His foreskin', the word in the פסוק that the drasha is built on

steps.confusionAlert: Saying his מילה does not override שבת does not mean an אנדרוגינוס is exempt from מילה. It only means it waits until after שבת.

phrases.english: 'His foreskin': a definite one overrides Shabbat,
but a hermaphrodite does not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: עׇרְלָתוֹ וַדַּאי דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת וְלֹא אַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same drasha to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the first תנא, the מילה of an אנדרוגינוס does not override שבת.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: an אנדרוגינוס's מילה does override שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees: an אנדרוגינוס is fully obligated in מילה, his מילה overrides שבת, and he gets כרת if he never has it done.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: [the מילה of] an אנדרוגינוס overrides שבת, and [if he stays uncircumcised] he is punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues with the first תנא. In his view an אנדרוגינוס counts as a full male for מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה an אנדרוגינוס is not a doubtful case at all. He is obligated, so his מילה overrides שבת, and as an adult he would even be liable for כרת if he stays uncircumcised. This leaves the word ערלתו free to teach other cases, which come in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion
Punished with כרת, being cut off spiritually

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
a hermaphrodite overrides Shabbat,
and he is punishable by karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the ruling of step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אנדרוגינוס is fully obligated in מילה. It overrides שבת, and failing to do it carries כרת.

steps.title: A baby born בין השמשות is not circumcised on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses ערלתו to exclude a baby born בין השמשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'ערלתו': a definite [case] overrides שבת, but one born בין השמשות does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רבי יהודה does not need ערלתו for the אנדרוגינוס, he uses it for a baby born בין השמשות, the twilight time when we do not know which day it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a baby is born at twilight, we do not know which day was the birth day. So we cannot be sure which day is really the eighth. Since it is unclear whether שבת is the correct day, his מילה does not push aside שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight; the doubtful time between day and night
Was born

phrases.english: 'His foreskin': a definite one overrides Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא נוֹלָד בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: but one born at twilight does not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא נוֹלָד בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה redirects the drasha to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby born בין השמשות is not circumcised on שבת.

steps.title: A baby born circumcised is not circumcised on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A second exclusion from ערלתו: a baby born with no visible foreskin.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'ערלתו': a definite [foreskin] overrides שבת, but one born circumcised does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא learns another case from the word ערלתו: a baby born already looking circumcised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no clear foreskin here to cut. So whatever is done for him, such as drawing a drop of blood, is not strong enough to push aside שבת. The next step explains that what to do for such a baby is itself a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: Born already circumcised, with no visible foreskin

phrases.english: 'His foreskin': a definite one overrides Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא נוֹלָד כְּשֶׁהוּא מָהוּל דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: but one born circumcised does not override Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא נוֹלָד כְּשֶׁהוּא מָהוּל דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second application of the same drasha.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby born מהול is not treated with מילה on שבת.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about a baby born circumcised
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains why this baby is a doubtful case: בית שמאי require drawing דם ברית, and בית הלל do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: For בית שמאי say: one must drip covenant blood from him; and בית הלל say: it is not necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the background for step 5. There is a מחלוקת about what, if anything, must be done for a baby born circumcised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that a drop of דם ברית must be drawn in place of the מילה. בית הלל say nothing at all is needed. Since even the need for this act is in dispute, it certainly cannot push aside שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: To draw a drop of covenant blood (a symbolic מילה)
The school of שמאי
The school of הלל

phrases.english: For Beit Shammai say:
one must drip covenant blood from him,
and Beit Hillel say: it is not necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁבֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים צָרִיךְ לְהַטִּיף מִמֶּנּוּ דַּם בְּרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a baby born מהול: בית שמאי require הטפת דם ברית, and בית הלל do not.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: everyone agrees a baby born circumcised needs blood drawn
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about this baby. Both agree דם ברית is needed, because the foreskin may just be hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not disagree about one born circumcised, that one must drip covenant blood from him, because it is a hidden foreskin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives a different version of the מחלוקת. He says that for a baby born circumcised, both schools require drawing blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is ערלה כבושה: the foreskin may really be there, just pressed down and hidden. So the baby may not truly be circumcised. Both schools therefore agree that a drop of blood must be drawn.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who reports a different version of the מחלוקת
A hidden foreskin, pressed down so it is not visible
They did not disagree

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about one born circumcised,
that one must drip covenant blood from him,
because it is a hidden foreskin.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the version of the מחלוקת given in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees that a baby born מהול needs הטפת דם ברית, because of ערלה כבושה.

steps.title: The real dispute: a convert who was already circumcised
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, the מחלוקת is about a גר who was circumcised before he converted.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what did they disagree? About a convert who converted when already circumcised. בית שמאי say: one must drip covenant blood from him; and בית הלל say: one need not drip covenant blood from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר now tells us where the מחלוקת really applies: a non-Jew who was already circumcised and then converts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no hidden foreskin. His מילה was done, but not for the sake of the ברית. בית שמאי still require a drop of דם ברית. בית הלל say it is not needed, and he only needs טבילה to complete his conversion.

keyTerms.meaning: About what did they disagree?
A convert who converted

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?
About a convert who converted when already circumcised,
for Beit Shammai say:
one must drip covenant blood from him,
and Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין צָרִיךְ לְהַטִּיף מִמֶּנּוּ דַּם בְּרִית.
phrases.english: one need not drip covenant blood from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מַה נֶּחְלְקוּ עַל גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר כְּשֶׁהוּא מָהוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version of the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a גר who was already circumcised: בית שמאי require הטפת דם ברית, and בית הלל do not.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל. In רבי יהודה's version they argue about a baby born מהול. In רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's version, everyone agrees that baby needs blood drawn (ערלה כבושה), and the argument is only about a גר who was already circumcised.

steps.title: Which case does 'doubtful' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא's line that a ספק does not override שבת and asks what case it is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמר מר: and a doubtful [case] does not override שבת. What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now begins its own discussion of the ברייתא. It quotes the line from step 1 and asks which doubtful case is meant, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first תנא's statement, ספק is listed next to the אנדרוגינוס, but no specific case of doubt is named. The baby born at twilight appears only in רבי יהודה's statement. So the גמרא asks which concrete case of doubt this general word ספק is meant to include.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said': the formula for quoting an earlier source in order to discuss it
'To include what?': which case does this come to add?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: וְלֹא סָפֵק דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: The Master said: and a doubtful [case] does not override Shabbat.
phrases.notes: The גמרא really does repeat the line here, because it is about to analyze it.

phrases.english: What does it come to include?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר וְלֹא סָפֵק דּוֹחֶה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the line in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific doubtful case is included by the words 'ולא ספק'?

steps.title: It includes a baby who may be a seven-month or an eight-month birth
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a baby who might be a בן שמונה (who in their view is not expected to survive) is not circumcised on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: To include what רבנן taught: for a בן שבעה, we desecrate שבת; for a בן שמונה, we do not desecrate שבת; for a baby who may be a בן שבעה or may be a בן שמונה, we do not desecrate שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 9. ספק refers to a baby when we are not sure whether he was born in the seventh month or the eighth month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In their understanding, a בן שבעה is expected to live, so we do his מילה on שבת. A בן שמונה was assumed not to survive, so we do not break שבת for him. When we are unsure which one he is, we treat him as doubtful and do not break שבת for his מילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby born after seven months, considered able to live
A baby born after eight months, assumed in their time not to survive
We break שבת for him (here, for his מילה)
That which רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: The ספק excluded by the word ערלתו is a baby who might be a בן שמונה. His מילה waits until after שבת.

phrases.english: To include that which the Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן שִׁבְעָה, מְחַלְּלִין עָלָיו אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: for a seven-month baby, we desecrate Shabbat for him.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֶן שְׁמוֹנָה, אֵין מְחַלְּלִין עָלָיו אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: But for an eight-month baby, we do not desecrate Shabbat for him.

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק בֶּן שִׁבְעָה סָפֵק בֶּן שְׁמוֹנָה —
phrases.english: If it is doubtful whether he is seven-month or eight-month,
we do not desecrate Shabbat for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵתוֹיֵי הָא דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ולא ספק' includes a baby who may be a בן שבעה or a בן שמונה. We do not break שבת for his מילה.

steps.title: A baby born in the eighth month is treated like a stone
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that a בן שמונה baby is like a stone and may not be moved on שבת. His mother may still bend over and nurse him because of danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: A baby born in the eighth month is like a stone, and it is forbidden to move him. But his mother may bend over him and nurse him, because of the danger.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues talking about the בן שמונה baby from the last step. It gives a second rule: he may not be carried on שבת, but he may be nursed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's view a בן שמונה is not expected to live, so for שבת purposes he is treated like an object with no use, like a stone, which is מוקצה. Nursing is still allowed. The mother bends over him rather than lifting him, and the 'danger' is to her, since built-up milk can make her sick.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a stone: treated as a useless object for שבת purposes
To move him (the מוקצה prohibition)
Bends over
Because of the danger (here, to the mother's health)

steps.confusionAlert: The mother does not pick the baby up. She bends over him to nurse, so the rule against moving him stays in place.

phrases.english: A baby born in the eighth month is like a stone,
and it is forbidden to move him.
phrases.notes: He is treated as מוקצה on שבת.

phrases.english: But his mother may bend over and nurse him
because of the danger.
phrases.notes: The danger is to the mother, whose milk would otherwise build up painfully.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן שְׁמוֹנָה הֲרֵי הוּא כְּאֶבֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another halacha about the same בן שמונה baby mentioned in the answer of Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בן שמונה is מוקצה like a stone and may not be moved, but his mother may bend over and nurse him because of danger.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about whose explanation is the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: רב rules like the תנא קמא, and שמואל rules like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, about a baby born circumcised.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב said the הלכה follows the תנא קמא. שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the baby born circumcised and reports an argument between two אמוראים about which explanation of the ברייתא is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the תנא קמא, בית שמאי and בית הלל argued about this baby, and we follow בית הלל, so no דם ברית is needed. רב rules this way. According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, everyone agrees דם ברית is needed. שמואל rules this way, so for him the baby must have דם ברית drawn.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated: introduces an argument between אמוראים
The first תנא. Here it means the opinion stated before רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: רבי יהודה's version, in which בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about a baby born circumcised.
The practical ruling follows...

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument sets up the story that follows. רב אדא בר אהבה will act like שמואל and later regret not following רב.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav said:
The halacha follows the first tanna,
phrases.notes: For a baby born circumcised, no דם ברית is needed (following בית הלל).

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.
phrases.notes: Everyone agrees דם ברית is needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר רַב אָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about the בן שמונה and returns to the main question of the baby born circumcised.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: no דם ברית is needed for a baby born circumcised. שמואל: דם ברית is needed.

steps.title: The story of רב אדא בר אהבה's son
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה had a son born circumcised. He asked thirteen מוהלים, who refused because it was שבת. He did it himself, and the baby ended up with a כרות שפכה. רב אדא said he deserved this for going against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה had a baby born already circumcised. He went around to thirteen מוהלים, until the baby ended up with a severed urethra. He said: 'I deserve this, because I went against רב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real case. רב אדא tried to draw דם ברית from his son, as שמואל rules, and it ended badly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא acted like שמואל and drew דם ברית on שבת. When the baby was injured, he saw it as a punishment for not following רב, who says no דם ברית is needed at all. This raises a question, which the next step asks.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby
Circumcised
מוהלים (those who perform circumcision)
One whose urethra is severed (a serious injury)
It should come upon me, meaning 'I deserve this'

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava
had a certain baby born to him
already circumcised.
He went around to thirteen circumcisers,
phrases.notes: The case took place on שבת.

phrases.english: until he was made one with a severed urethra.
He said: Let it come upon me (I deserve this),
since I went against Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אִתְיְלִיד לֵיהּ הָהוּא יָנוֹקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practical case of the רב and שמואל argument from Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אדא drew דם ברית like שמואל, the baby was injured, and he regretted not following רב.

steps.title: רב נחמן: You went against שמואל too
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges רב אדא. Even שמואל only required דם ברית on a weekday, not on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Didn't you go against שמואל too? Say that שמואל said this on a weekday. Did he say it on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רב אדא's words, 'I went against רב.' He says רב אדא went against שמואל as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if דם ברית is needed, the reason is only a doubt that the foreskin is hidden. In Step 1 the ברייתא taught that a ספק does not override שבת. So even שמואל would not allow drawing blood on שבת, and רב אדא went against both.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he not go against שמואל?
Say (granted that...)
On a weekday

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying שמואל disagrees with drawing דם ברית. He grants (אימר) that שמואל requires it on a weekday and argues that this does not extend to שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
And did he not go against Shmuel too?!
Say that Shmuel said this on a weekday;
on Shabbat, did he say it?
phrases.notes: Since it is only a ספק, it should not override שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן וְאַדִּשְׁמוּאֵל לָא עֲבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אדא's statement in Step 13 that he went only against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא's claim that he went only against רב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's requirement of דם ברית is based on a doubt, and a doubt does not override שבת. So on שבת, even שמואל would forbid it.

steps.title: רב אדא held the hidden foreskin is a certainty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב אדא held this baby surely has a hidden foreskin, so the case is not a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He held that it is certainly a hidden foreskin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אדא against רב נחמן's challenge by explaining what רב אדא believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hidden foreskin is a certainty, drawing דם ברית is a real, definite מילה. A definite מילה does override שבת. So under שמואל's view he did nothing wrong, and his only regret was not following רב.

keyTerms.meaning: He held (this was his view)
Certainly
A hidden foreskin, pressed in so that it is not visible

phrases.english: He held,
it is certainly a hidden foreskin.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא סָבַר וַדַּאי עׇרְלָה כְּבוּשָׁה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge from Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case from a doubt to a certainty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Drawing דם ברית is only because of a doubt, so it cannot override שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב אדא held the hidden foreskin is certain, so the מילה is definite and overrides שבת.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף argue: doubt or certainty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב אדא's view is a known opinion. רבה says we only worry that a foreskin is hidden, while רב יוסף says it is certainly hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: רבה said, we are concerned that perhaps it is a hidden foreskin. רב יוסף said, it is certainly a hidden foreskin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by quoting an argument between אמוראים. רב אדא followed רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, the case is a ספק, so it does not override שבת, and רב נחמן's challenge would hold. According to רב יוסף, it is certain, so the מילה overrides שבת. This shows that רב אדא's position has a source.

keyTerms.meaning: We are concerned (it is only a doubt)
Perhaps
As it was stated: introduces a supporting source

steps.whatToRemember: For a baby born circumcised: רב says no דם ברית is needed, and שמואל says it is. On שבת it depends on רבה and רב יוסף. If the hidden foreskin is only a doubt (רבה), we do not draw blood on שבת. If it is certain (רב יוסף), we do.

phrases.english: As it was stated: Rabba said:
We are concerned that perhaps it is a hidden foreskin.
phrases.notes: Only a doubt, so it does not override שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is certainly a hidden foreskin.
phrases.notes: A certainty, so it overrides שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר רַבָּה אָמַר חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא עׇרְלָה כְּבוּשָׁה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in Step 15 by showing that the 'certainty' view is רב יוסף's opinion.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that some hold the hidden foreskin is a certainty
steps.raayaSupportSource: The argument between רבה and רב יוסף

steps.title: רב יוסף brings a proof from רבי אליעזר הקפר
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites רבי אליעזר הקפר, who says בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about חילול שבת. He infers that the תנא קמא held one may desecrate שבת, which fits his view that the foreskin is certainly hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: How do I know my view? From a ברייתא. רבי אליעזר הקפר says: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about a baby born circumcised. Both agree you must draw a drop of דם ברית from him. They argued only about whether you may break שבת for him. בית שמאי say you may break שבת for him, and בית הלל say you may not. Doesn't this show that the תנא קמא held you may break שבת for him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a source to back up his view from the last step, that a baby born circumcised certainly has a hidden foreskin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר הקפר moves the argument to a different question than the תנא קמא did. רב יוסף infers that the תנא קמא must hold that breaking שבת is allowed. You would only break שבת for a real מילה, so the hidden foreskin must be a certainty and not a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a proof for one's own view)
To draw a drop of covenant blood
To desecrate שבת (doing מלאכה for the מילה)
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
By inference, from what is implied

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר הקפר himself does not say anything about the תנא קמא's view on שבת. רב יוסף is reading it in by inference, which is why the next step can question it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ —
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: From where do I say this?
As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer HaKappar says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about one born already circumcised
that one must draw covenant blood from him.

phrases.aramaic: עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ — לְחַלֵּל עָלָיו אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: About what did they disagree? About desecrating Shabbat for him.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים מְחַלְּלִין עָלָיו אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: One desecrates Shabbat for him,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מְחַלְּלִין עָלָיו אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: One does not desecrate Shabbat for him.
Does this not imply that the first tanna holds
that one desecrates Shabbat for him?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יוסף supports his own view from step 16 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view that a baby born circumcised certainly has a hidden foreskin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר הקפר, plus the inference about the תנא קמא's view on חילול שבת.

steps.title: Maybe the תנא קמא held no one may desecrate שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another way to read the ברייתא. Perhaps the תנא קמא held that everyone agrees you may not break שבת, which would undo רב יוסף's proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the תנא קמא was saying that everyone agrees you may not break שבת for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב יוסף's proof by offering a different reading of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא קמא held that nobody allows breaking שבת, then the תנא קמא treats the hidden foreskin as only a doubt. In that case רבי אליעזר הקפר would be the one adding a view that allows it. The inference no longer supports רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces another possible reading)
Everyone agrees

phrases.english: But perhaps the first tanna
is saying that all agree one does not desecrate!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא תַּנָּא קַמָּא דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין מְחַלְּלִין קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference רב יוסף drew in step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the inference about the תנא קמא's view, not the ברייתא itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can also be read so that the תנא קמא forbids breaking שבת.

steps.title: Why would רבי אליעזר הקפר come just to teach בית שמאי's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the pushback. On that reading, רבי אליעזר הקפר's only new point would be בית שמאי's opinion, and the הלכה does not follow בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, did רבי אליעזר הקפר come just to teach us the reasoning of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading it just offered in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On step 18's reading, רבי אליעזר הקפר's whole new point is that someone, namely בית שמאי, allows breaking שבת. But the הלכה follows בית הלל. A תנא would not bother bringing a new statement just to teach a view we do not follow.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
He came to teach us

phrases.english: If so, Rabbi Eliezer HaKappar
came to teach us the reasoning of Beit Shammai?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הַקַּפָּר טַעְמָא דְבֵית שַׁמַּאי אֲתָא לְאַשְׁמוֹעִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דחיה of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 18, that the תנא קמא holds everyone forbids breaking שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading leaves רבי אליעזר הקפר's only new point as בית שמאי's opinion, which has no practical use.

steps.title: Perhaps he means they did not disagree about this matter at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reading רבי אליעזר הקפר's words differently. He means that בית שמאי and בית הלל agree about שבת, so רב יוסף's proof still does not hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this is what he means: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not disagree about this matter of breaking שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 19 and keeps alive the doubt about רב יוסף's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reading is that רבי אליעזר הקפר is not adding a view that allows breaking שבת. He is saying that both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree you do not break שבת, and their argument is only about drawing blood on a weekday. So he is not teaching בית שמאי's view, and רב יוסף's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is saying (a reinterpretation)
In this matter

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's proof from רבי אליעזר הקפר is not conclusive. The ברייתא can be read so that no one allows breaking שבת for a baby born circumcised.

phrases.english: Perhaps this is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל בְּדָבָר זֶה.
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree about this matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִילְמָא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 and keeps the דחיה of step 18 standing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר הקפר was adding a view that allows breaking שבת, which would be בית שמאי's.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר הקפר says both sides agree about שבת, so the proof for רב יוסף is not compelling.

steps.title: רבי אסי: the eighth-day rule depends on the mother's birth impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי teaches that only a baby whose birth makes his mother טמאה לידה is circumcised on the eighth day. He learns this from the פסוק in ויקרא that places the two laws side by side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: Any baby whose mother becomes טמאה from giving birth is circumcised on the eighth day. Any baby whose mother does not become טמאה from the birth, such as a birth by surgery, is not tied to the eighth day. As the פסוק says: 'If a woman conceives and gives birth to a male, she shall be impure... and on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי אסי states a rule linking the eighth-day מילה to the mother's טומאת לידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה puts the mother's טומאה and the baby's eighth-day מילה in the same passage. רבי אסי reads them as connected. When there is no טומאת לידה, the special eighth-day timing does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure because of childbirth
Circumcised on the eighth day
Conceives (literally 'bears seed')
His foreskin

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אסי does not say such a baby has no מילה at all. He says only that the fixed eighth-day timing does not apply to him.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁאִמּוֹ טְמֵאָה לֵידָה — נִימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה,
phrases.english: Any whose mother is impure from childbirth is circumcised on the eighth,
and any whose mother is not impure from childbirth
is not circumcised on the eighth,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אִשָּׁה כִּי תַזְרִיעַ וְיָלְדָה זָכָר וְטָמְאָה וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: as it says: 'If a woman conceives and bears a male, she shall be impure, etc.'
'and on the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי כׇּל שֶׁאִמּוֹ טְמֵאָה לֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new subject, the eighth-day timing of מילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eighth-day obligation of מילה depends on the mother becoming טמאה לידה.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבי אסי from the early generations
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that before מתן תורה there was no טומאת לידה, yet babies were still circumcised on the eighth day. This seems to break רבי אסי's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The early generations prove otherwise. Their mothers were not טמאה from giving birth, yet the babies were circumcised on the eighth day!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבי אסי's rule with a counter-example from history.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From אברהם until הר סיני, the laws of טומאת לידה had not yet been given. Even so, the תורה in בראשית commands מילה on the eighth day. So the eighth day does not seem to depend on the mother's טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The early generations, before מתן תורה
They will prove (a counter-example)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
The early generations will prove it,
for the mother was not impure from childbirth,
and yet he was circumcised on the eighth!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: דּוֹרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים יוֹכִיחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי אסי's rule from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's rule that the eighth-day מילה depends on טומאת לידה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Before סיני there was no טומאת לידה, yet eighth-day מילה applied, so the two cannot depend on each other.

steps.title: רבי אסי begins his answer by pointing to מתן תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי starts to answer אביי by pointing to מתן תורה as a turning point. The answer is only opened here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said to him: When the Torah was given,
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי begins to answer אביי's question about the babies born before מתן תורה. This line sets up the answer, which is completed on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's challenge assumed that the rules before מתן תורה should prove what the rules are after it. By opening with "when the Torah was given," רבי אסי signals that he will separate the two time periods. The case from before מתן תורה would then not disprove his rule for after it.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him. Here it introduces רבי אסי's reply to אביי.
The תורה was given. This refers to מתן תורה at הר סיני.

steps.confusionAlert: The answer is not finished yet. Do not decide what רבי אסי means until you see the rest of his reply on the next amud.

phrases.english: He (Rabbi Asi) said to him (Abaye):
phrases.notes: This introduces the reply to אביי's challenge from Step 22.

phrases.english: When the Torah was given,
phrases.notes: This opens a sentence that continues on the next amud. It marks מתן תורה as the turning point.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It directly answers אביי's קשיא in Step 22 against רבי אסי's rule in Step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the time periods: the law before מתן תורה is set apart from the law after it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי assumed that the eighth-day מילה before מתן תורה, when there was no טומאת לידה, disproves the link between the two laws.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer begins by marking מתן תורה as the point where the law changed. Its full wording follows on the next amud.
